 Hon'ble Smt. Justice Rajani Dubey

1.

This application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No. 55/2022 registered at Police Station- Chando, District- Balrampur-Ramanujganj (C.G.) for commission of the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 450, 506 of the IPC.

2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the complainant lodged a written complaint alleging therein that when the prosecutrix went to weave twine at 4:00 am, in the month of June, where the applicant was already weaving twine, then he came to her suddenly from behind caught her when she tried to scream, then choked her mouth with his hands and forced her to do wrong by throwing her on the ground and threatened her to disclosed about the incident to anyone. Thereafter, about 15 days later, when she went to the forest to graze goats, then around 12:00 O'clock in the day the accused caught her from behind and forced her to commit wrong in the forest.

It is also alleged that on 27.10.2022 when she was taking bath by closing the door of her house at that time the accused asked to open the door and she denied opening it then he entered by jumping the handle and committing wrong by taking her to the kitchen.

Based on this, offence has been registered against Abdul Ajeej Ansari vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12801056/
1 the present applicant.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the present applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this case.

He next submits that the applicant is a 55-year-old man and he lent Rs. 1,00,000/- to the husband of the prosecutrix about one year ago and they had promised to return the same within a period of six months.
When the applicant demanded the said amount from the husband of the prosecutrix they started refusing to return the same.
Based on this, a false report has been lodged against the present applicant.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate security and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Hon'ble Court.
Therefore, the present applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, counsel for the State opposes the application for anticipatory bail.

5. After hearing counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in particular, the quality of the evidence and considering the age of the applicant, this Court is of the considered opinion that it is a fit case to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, the application is allowed.
It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with aforesaid crime number, he shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety for the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned arresting/investigating officer or the Court concerned, as the case may be, with the following terms and conditions:
(i) that the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation before the concerned investigating officer as and when required;
(ii) that the applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts or the case as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(iii) that the applicant shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial; and (iv) that the applicant shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial Sd/-
